```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
here::i_am("coppock_2016_errata.qmd")
```

```{r entries}
# THE ERRATA SPINE for the corrigendum, kept apart from errata.qmd's because the
# corrigendum is a separately published article with its own DOI and its own numbering.
# Every entry is defined once, here, and rendered from here: into this document, and into
# whatever else needs it, which reads the coppock_2016_errata_entries.csv written at the
# bottom of this file rather than keeping a second hand-typed copy.
#
# [[...]] marks the span that changes. Each renderer supplies its own markup for it: bold
# here, \was{} in an edition. Nothing else in a field is markup, so the same string can be
# set by either.
#
# Numbering is APPEND-ONLY once this note is published: an entry can already have been
# cited, so a later finding is added at the end and never interleaved.
#
# claim_ids names the ground-truth rows an entry corrects, semicolon-separated.
entries <- tribble(
  ~entry, ~class, ~source, ~form, ~title, ~location, ~published, ~corrected, ~note, ~claim_ids,

  1, "quantity", "pipeline", "brief",
  "None of the four upper confidence bounds is the one the data support",
  "published pp. 206--207",
  "with 95% confidence intervals extending from -0.325 to [[-0.025]] for the indirect effect and -0.575 to [[0.000]] for the direct effect. [...] The 95% confidence intervals are much wider, at [-0.325, [[0.200]]] for the indirect effect and [-0.625, [[0.175]]] for the direct effect",
  "with 95% confidence intervals extending from -0.325 to [[-0.050]] for the indirect effect and -0.575 to [[-0.025]] for the direct effect. [...] The 95% confidence intervals are much wider, at [-0.325, [[0.175]]] for the indirect effect and [-0.625, [[0.200 or higher]]] for the direct effect",
  paste("The bounds are read off the p-value surfaces saved in the corrigendum's own",
        "archive (doi:10.7910/DVN/H47CC6, fig2.rdata), the original panel for the first",
        "pair of intervals and the corrected panel for the second. The function that",
        "located them returned the first grid point after each edge of the confidence",
        "region, which is the first point inside at the lower edge and the first point",
        "outside at the upper edge, so three of the four upper bounds sit one step of",
        "0.025 too high. The fourth, the corrected direct bound, lies at the top of the",
        "grid searched: the region runs to 0.2, where the function returns no bound at",
        "all, so the printed 0.175 has no origin in the code, and the data place the",
        "bound no lower than 0.2. The lower bounds are correct. Corrected, the original",
        "intervals still exclude zero and the corrected ones still include it, which is",
        "the corrigendum's conclusion."),
  "corr_orig_indirect_ci_upper; corr_orig_direct_ci_upper; corr_new_indirect_ci_upper; corr_new_direct_ci_upper",

  2, "text", "reading", "brief",
  "A name in the acknowledgments is misspelled",
  "published p. 208",
  "I am grateful to Peter M. Aronow, Jake Bowers, and Mark M. [[Frederickson]]",
  "I am grateful to Peter M. Aronow, Jake Bowers, and Mark M. [[Fredrickson]]",
  "The corrigendum's own reference list spells the name correctly, in Bowers, Fredrickson, and Panagopoulos (2013).",
  NA,

  3, "text", "reading", "brief",
  "A reference gives the wrong second author",
  "published p. 208, references",
  "Butler, D. M., and [[David, W. N.]] (2011). Can learning constituency opinion affect how legislators vote?",
  "Butler, D. M., and [[Nickerson, D. W.]] (2011). Can learning constituency opinion affect how legislators vote?",
  paste("The second author of the experiment the article reanalyzes is David W. Nickerson,",
        "whose given and family names the printed entry reverses. The 2014 article",
        "cites the same paper correctly."),
  NA
) |>
  mutate(across(c(title, published, corrected, note, claim_ids), as.character))

stopifnot(nrow(entries) == max(entries$entry), !anyDuplicated(entries$entry))

spell <- function(n) {
  words <- c("one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight", "nine", "ten")
  stopifnot(n >= 1, n <= length(words))
  words[n]
}

# The spine's markup, resolved for this document. Another renderer resolves it differently.
bold <- function(x) str_replace_all(x, "\\[\\[(.*?)\\]\\]", "**\\1**")
```

This note lists `r spell(nrow(entries))` corrections to the corrigendum to "Information Spillovers: Another Look at Experimental Estimates of Legislator Responsiveness," published in *Journal of Experimental Political Science* 3(2):206--208, doi [10.1017/XPS.2016.8](https://doi.org/10.1017/XPS.2016.8). **None changes the corrigendum's conclusion.** The first moves four upper confidence bounds, and both corrected intervals still include zero; the other two are names.

The corrigendum corrects Coppock (2014), *Journal of Experimental Political Science* 1(2):159--169, doi [10.1017/xps.2014.9](https://doi.org/10.1017/xps.2014.9), which has an errata note of its own. The data and code behind the corrigendum are deposited at doi [10.7910/DVN/H47CC6](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/H47CC6), and the maintained analysis that reproduces it is at [github.com/active-maintenance-aec/coppock_2014](https://github.com/active-maintenance-aec/coppock_2014).

# The text

```{r text-entries, results="asis"}
# A heading is only a heading when a blank line precedes it, which is why every emitted
# entry opens with one.
walk(entries$entry, function(n) {
  e <- entries |> filter(entry == n)
  cat("\n\n## ", e$entry, ". ", e$title, "\n\nPublished, ",
      str_remove(e$location, "^published "), ":\n\n> ", bold(e$published),
      "\n\nCorrected:\n\n> ", bold(e$corrected), "\n\n", e$note, "\n", sep = "")
})
```

```{r emit-spine}
# The machine-readable spine, written wherever this document is rendered. Anything else
# that needs these entries reads it rather than keeping its own copy, so the two cannot
# drift.
write_csv(entries, here("coppock_2016_errata_entries.csv"))
```
